title: Issues with New "firefly" G6 transmitter (serial# 8G... or 8H...)
body: Recieved two new transmitters for my dexcom G6 with serial numbers beginning in 8G. Attempted multiple times to follow instructions listed here https://androidaps.readthedocs.io/en/latest/EN/Configuration/xdrip.html but with no success. I will sometimes recieved a few minutes of reading but eventually xdrips+ will no longer report current values. Please help! Really need this to work for an upcoming triathlon!

comments.body: Same for me.
Which xDrip+ version are you using? If not very recent please switch to Alpha update channel and try that.

So I have just started today my 8G Transmitter with the latest Alpha version of xDrip+ and in the beginning, for about 3hrs it collected the date and then suddenly stopped. 
The Dexcom Receiver still works, but xDrip does not connect since hours. restarted phone, bluetooth, collector and everything but nothing works.
With the 80 Transmitter used till today it worked quite well, so the problem has to be with the 8G one.

ok, so after 3hrs - just after this comment - I tried a step I read somewhere else and now I have at least 1 new data. 
On the system status screen I clicked on "forget device" and restarted the data collector. Not sure if that helped any or if it was just coincidence.
I also got some backfill of data, which is nice, though it was pretty annyoing to not have any update for 3hrs.
Not sure what more information you need for bug tracing?

Hello,

if I see it correctly I already got the new transmitter. But I have no issues using a Sony Xperia XZ1 Android 9. Only thing special. It has no service. I use it offline without a SIM Card.

My procedure to start the sensor:
1) Stop the old one and wait until it is stopped. 
               Queue must be empty under status.

<This is special, no need if only xdrip is used>
_I have an iPhone 8 with the Dexcom app, which I use as backup. Bluetooth is forbidden for Dexcom. Therefor I stop the sensor in the Dexcom app, too. I switch on Bluetooth for the Dexcom App and start the sensor.  Without waiting for the App to connect I switch of Bluetooth and block it again for the Dexcom app._ 
<xDrip+>
2) I start a new sensor in xDrip and enter Code. 
3) Wait for the warmup to finish. During this yDrip will connect to the sensor and you see the countdown.
4)Working
<This is special, no need if only xdrip is used>
  _The iPhone must stay disconnected to the sensor during its warm up. If the warm up is done, I can switch between xDrip on Android and Dexcom on the iPhone. Of course only one at the same time_

Similar problems here. Tried running an 8H transmitter. Unfortunately I was not in a spot to capture and post logs, etc. I am running Android 9. 

I was running latest nightly build from 29 Jan. Had initial connection to the 8H and then started to be intermittent. Had to give that up due to traveling schedule and need for solid readings.

That 8H Transmitter now only connects to the Dexcom Receiver. It seems that somehow, the transmitter did not release its second bluetooth slot, creating a pairing problem. No luck even after restarting  phone, factory resetting phone, faraday bagging the transmitter and more of the tricks found on various websites. 

Other observation: So far, in my experience, I've found if you stop a G6 sensor from the Dexcom Receiver, there is no way to restart it, so try to avoid that option until the last possible moment if you can. 

If/when I have another go at this with an 8H, I will share logs, etc.

(Thanks so much to the xdrip team for all that you do. Simply amazing.)

I'm glad it's working for some people. It's not working for a lot of us. Are there any solutions yet? We have Android 9 on a Google Pixel, most recent nightly build. Ours works for about 12 hours then stops connecting.

@nshtg Are you running the Dexcom receiver with your 8H transmitter at all? Or only an android device (phone or watch) with xdrip?

While it doesn't help those of us that really, really want to get back on xdrip with our firefly transmitters, this may not be an xdrip-specific issue. The culprit might, in fact, be buggy firefly transmitter bluetooth connectivity issues.

FWIW: a new 8H failed following the Dexcom process, using their phone app and receiver. Perhaps in their valiant attempts to lock down the transmitter and discourage unofficial 3rd party apps, they have created their own problems? A bit like creating home security that works so well, the bad people can't get in but you also can't get out. 

8H failure using Dexcom's receiver and app were all similar to issues described here and on the Dexcom reddit community - transmitter connects to Dexcom receiver fine but loses connection to the phone running the Dexcom phone app and cannot re-connect. It seems like there's something buggy with the firefly transmitter's bluetooth to the phone but not to their receivers. Could their receiver lock on the first connection and the second bluetooth connection to the phone is the flaky one or the receiver connection is somehow interfering? They asked for the transmitter back for troubleshooting. Standard protocol for them. Also, they're now up to 8K transmitter series and will run out of letters before we know it.

Maybe there's a nugget in the above that can help in troubleshooting.

Hopefully this will get sorted sooner rather than later.

so for me the Dexcom App is working just fine without any interupts, even if connected as third "party" (after xDrip stopped working and got de-installed). Of course the Dexcom app was not on my phone during the usage of xDrip. So I don't suspect any bluetooth issues with the transmitter to be the problem...
